message.content:
When it comes to jazz vocalists, several names stand out as iconic and highly influential. While “best” can be subjective and depends on personal taste, here are a few artists who are widely regarded as among the greatest:

| Artist | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and phrasing set a standard for jazz vocal technique. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her emotive delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into deeply personal statements; she’s often cited as one of the most emotionally powerful singers. |
| **Louis Armstrong** | Though primarily a trumpeter, his charismatic voice and pioneering recordings helped bring jazz to a broader audience. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | A modern torch‑song specialist whose phrasing and emotional depth echo the greats of the past. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A contemporary artist blending classic jazz sensibilities with modern storytelling. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best,” many critics and fans point to **Ella Fitzgerald** for her technical brilliance and lasting influence. However, each of these artists brings something unique to the genre, so exploring their catalogs will give you a richer sense of what makes a jazz vocalist truly great.
